items.solution_latex: Separate: \frac{dy}{y} = 2dx. Integrate: \ln|y| = 2x + C, \text{ so } y = Ae^{2x}. Apply y(0) = 3: 3 = A e^{0} \Rightarrow A = 3. \text{ Final answer: } y = 3e^{2x}.
hint_ladder: Remember to integrate both sides before applying the initial condition.
After finding the general solution, substitute the initial condition to find the constant.
items.targets_because: This item requires the student to separate and integrate before applying the initial condition, isolating the misconception.

items.solution_latex: Separate: \frac{dy}{y} = 3x^2 dx. Integrate: \ln|y| = x^3 + C, \text{ so } y = Ae^{x^3}. Apply y(1) = 4: 4 = Ae^{1} \Rightarrow A = 4e^{-1}. \text{ Final answer: } y = 4e^{-1} e^{x^3} = 4e^{x^3 - 1}.
hint_ladder: Integrate both sides before substituting the initial condition.
Use the initial condition to solve for the constant after finding the general solution.
items.targets_because: This item emphasizes the importance of integrating before applying the initial condition, addressing the misconception directly.
